The old lighthouse stood at the edge of the cliff for nearly 200 years. Every night, the keeper climbed the narrow stairs, cleaned the great glass lens, and lit the lamp that guided ships away from the rocks below. When the storms came in from the west, he would stay awake until dawn, listening to the wind and watching the dark water for any sign of trouble. Most of the sailors who passed never knew his name, but many of them owed him their lives. Today the light is automatic, and the keeper's cottage has become a small museum.
